findings.highlight: The unknown old man asks me such a question.
findings.evidenceJa: 正体不明の老人は快活に、物騒なコトを言ってくる。
findings.governingReading: The unidentified old man cheerfully says something menacing.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the breezy delivery and the dangerous content, flattening the contradiction that characterizes Zouken.

findings.highlight: your old man is pretty hard to deal with.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえのお爺ちゃんは、なかなかの難物だ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou privately calls Zouken Sakura’s grandfather and judges him a formidable or difficult person.
findings.explanation: Old man replaces the explicit family relation with a loose phrase that can mean father or husband in English.

findings.evidenceJa: ものすごくガッカリしているように見えて
findings.explanation: Shocked substitutes surprise for disappointment, changing why Shirou feels apologetic after failing Zouken’s expectation.

findings.highlight: The old man will go away, so please do not reserve yourself.
findings.evidenceJa: 年寄りは隠居しておるでな、気兼ねなく訪ねるがよい
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he is retired and secluded, so Shirou should visit the grandchildren without feeling constrained by him.
findings.explanation: Will go away invents an imminent departure and loses his stated household status; the following invitation is also malformed.
